The company

We make garments,
not promises.

Founded in 1999 in the Tiruppur cluster, where most of India's knitwear is made. We stayed here because the fabric, the dyeing, the trims and the labour are all within an hour of our gate.

Fabric arrives at our gate. Everything after that is ours.

We are a vertically integrated manufacturer of knitted and woven garments. Cutting, stitching, checking, ironing, packing and dispatch all happen inside our own unit at Kanakkampalayam, near Palladam. Nothing critical is handed to someone we cannot walk over to.

We supply international and domestic groups: brands in Canada, Germany, Poland, Greece, Spain and the Netherlands, and Indian labels sold through the country's largest marketplaces. Roughly 40% of what we ship is menswear, 35% womenswear and 25% kidswear.

Our team controls production, quality, planning and communication in-house, so the person answering your email is the person who can walk to the line and check.

The unit is 16,500 sq ft across four blocks, with 150 machines and around 250 people on the floor. That size is deliberate. It is large enough that a 100,000-piece tee programme does not disturb the nightwear line running beside it, and small enough that a supervisor, a merchandiser and the owner can stand at the same table and settle a fit comment the same afternoon.

When something drifts — a shade that moves between rolls, a measurement that creeps after wash — it is caught and corrected inside the same building. Garments are checked after stitching and again before packing, and the people who cut a style are a few steps from the people who pack it, which is why most corrections cost us a morning rather than a shipment.

Most of our volume is repeat business, so we plan the way a returning buyer needs us to: samples in one to two weeks, production in 45 days, shipment 45 to 60 days after confirmation, and a minimum of 1,000 pieces a style so a new programme can be proved before it scales. The floor is SMETA 4-Pillar audited and the business is Udyam-registered, and both documents go out with the first quotation instead of waiting to be asked for.

Checked at the source

Fabric is shade-checked and recorded against the lot before it is cut, so a shade problem never reaches a sewing line.

A stage, not an afterthought

Checking sits as its own section between stitching and finishing, with its own people and its own floor space.

Nothing ships unchecked

Final inspection happens before packing. Cartons are marked to buyer specification and staged in finished-goods storage.
